option_rescore_only.what_it_is: Replay the EXISTING recorded verdict files under a new evaluator id. The labels do not change, so no judging happens and no score moves; what changes is that each new evaluation carries the scenario-specific contract fingerprint.
option_rescore_only.caveat: It re-stamps rather than re-derives. It fixes the fingerprint defect and nothing else: cross-session judging drift, which the fingerprint never captured, stays exactly as it is in v1.0.

option_full_rejudge_recorded_route.what_it_is: Claude Opus 5 reading each response against the rubric in an interactive session and writing one labelled verdict per criterion, replayed with `evaluate --verdicts`. The budget item is supervised session time, not API tokens.
option_full_rejudge_recorded_route.comparison_point: The GLM 5.3 campaign produced 354 criterion verdicts for one model across the five scenarios. A full re-judge is that work times eight.

option_full_rejudge_api_route.why: This project has no Anthropic API key and no credits, and spending them is a hard rule violation rather than a cost trade-off. Every published MondayBench evaluation used route=recorded. Costed here only to size the alternative.

assumptions.why_no_data: JudgeRecord stores no token counts, and no evaluation was ever produced through the API route, so there is nothing historical to calibrate against.

estimated_cost_usd_range.note: input x $5.0/M and output x $15.0/M, the common frontier band. The repo pins no Opus 5 price, so this is a band, not a quote.

optional_provisional_rejudge.why: Their generations did not come through the official provider route - Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 are reachable only from the Claude Code subscription, whose system prompt and injected context are not the frozen ones (see audits/monday-002/fable-5.1-preflight.md). Re-judging them under v1.1 would make their EVALUATION comparable while their GENERATION still is not.
optional_provisional_rejudge.cost_if_ever_done: Two more models across five scenarios is 2/8 of the official re-judge, so roughly 713 further criterion verdicts on the same assumptions. It buys evaluation comparability for generations that remain non-comparable, which is why it is listed and not recommended.

honesty_note: There is no historical judge token data to calibrate against: JudgeRecord stores no token counts and every published evaluation used route=recorded, so the API figures are a sizing exercise built from measured prompt material and a stated chars-per-token assumption, not a quote.
